extracted.intended_audience: professional mathematicians and researchers interested in inter-universal Teichmüller theory, research verification, and scholarly communication
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for how to discuss, verify, and protect mathematical theories (especially inter-universal Teichmüller theory): emphasizes focusing on substantive mathematics, producing clear written logical documentation, respecting peer review, limiting reliance on non-expert media or naive computer checks, and engaging in constructive dialogue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentrate on substantive mathematical content
rubrics_metrics.description: to concentrate, in discussions of inter-universal Teichmüller theory, on substantive mathematical content, as opposed to non-mathematical — such as social, political, or psychological — aspects or interpretations of the situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid letting 'vicious spirals' of media/internet/social commentary dominate mathematical discourse; focus discussion on the underlying mathematics (cf. §1.8 and related remarks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce detailed, explicit, logically substantive, and readily accessible written documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: the production of detailed, explicit, mathematically substantive, and readily accessible written expositions of the logical structure underlying the assertions of the various parties involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such written documentation is presented as the only meaningful technical tool currently available to deal with fabricated/erroneous versions of a theory; serve as a transgenerational/transcultural common core and as protection against socio-political distortion (cf. §1.10 and repeated statements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof lies with proponents of modified/novel assertions
rubrics_metrics.description: the burden of proof of establishing any sort of logical relationship between such a modified version and the original version lies exclusively in the hands of the proponents of the modified version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assertions of ignorance of technical details do not justify participating in proliferation/citation/dissemination of modified versions (IgNoJst); proponents must provide rigorous linkage (BurPrf). Example: Pythagorean Theorem variants (Example 1.10.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect and rely on expert refereeing/peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: traditionally, detrimental effects from violations of mathematical intellectual property were typically averted in the field of mathematics by means of the refereeing systems of various well established mathematical journals; the burden of proof regarding correctness of novel assertions lies with the author of the manuscript containing the novel assertions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat media/internet commentary by non-experts as carrying more weight than thorough refereeing by experts (cf. §1.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Define and protect Mathematical Intellectual Property Rights (MIPRs)
rubrics_metrics.description: MIPRs: a notion modeled on conventional intellectual property, associated to mathematical notions and theories (not persons/corporations) and of unlimited duration; intended to protect the 'creditworthiness' of a mathematical notion/theory from severe injury caused by proliferation of logically unrelated fabricated 'fake' versions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize what constitutes a violation (VioMIPR) versus normal scholarly inquiry (Pyth1–Pyth3). Treat original labels and distinct versions correctly to avoid harmful confusion; historical role of refereeing in enforcing these norms is noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not prioritize mass media/internet commentary over formal validation
rubrics_metrics.description: grotesquely distorted mass media coverage and internet comments ... are regarded, in certain sectors of the mathematical community, as carrying much more weight than an exceptionally thorough refereeing process in a well established mathematical journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice is deeply regrettable and should be resisted; give precedence to substantive written exposition and expert review when resolving mathematical disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize limitations of computer verification for deep theories
rubrics_metrics.description: no computer verification algorithm for verifying some mathematical assertion can yield a verification of the validity of the algorithm itself, i.e., of the presumed relationship between the mechanical output yielded by the algorithm and the conventional human sense of 'mathematical correctness' (Algor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computer verification is useful for routine computations or finite/combinatorial settings, but cannot resolve confusions that stem from conflating fabricated versions with originals; therefore do not rely on automated verification alone for resolving these disputes (CmpVer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage in constructive mathematical dialogue with knowledgeable experts
rubrics_metrics.description: misunderstandings resulting from logically unrelated fabricated versions can only be overcome by studying the original papers ... or, if this is not sufficient, by engaging in constructive mathematical dialogue with mathematicians who do have a substantial, accurate understanding of the theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid 'refusal to engage' (RfsDlg) and use direct technical discussion as a remedy for misinformation; brief, focused exchanges can resolve technical questions (see student examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use transparent/symbolic representation of logical structure when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: the essential logical structure of any mathematical argument or theory can, in principle, be expressed in terms of elementary logical relations ... The symbolic representation ... is sufficiently simple and transparent that, once it has been properly communicated, it may be verified readily by mental computation in a matter of minutes without the use of a computer (SymIUT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize/compartmentalize complex 'blocks' into blackboxes and express the overall logical dependencies (AND/OR/NOT) symbolically to facilitate human verification and communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not disseminate or treat fabricated/logically unrelated versions as equivalent
rubrics_metrics.description: avoid the erroneous confusion of logically unrelated fabricated versions of a theory with the original version of the theory (this confusion completely invalidates the presumed relationship on which any sort of computer verification or meaningful resolution must be premised).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include RCS-IUT/OR-IUT/XOR-IUT vs original IUT; carefully track and respect distinct labels and their logical relations to avoid misleading the community (cf. (CmMth) and Example 1.10.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess travel/physical-meeting decisions by effort vs gain (geographical vs mathematical proximity)
rubrics_metrics.description: when, from the point of view of at least one of the key participants, the amount of effort, time, and/or money that must be expended to travel clearly exceeds, by a substantial margin — i.e., '≫' — the gain ... that appears likely to be obtained from the travel under consideration, it is highly probable that the travel under consideration will end up simply not taking place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that mathematical proximity (intellectual contact) can be more important than geographic proximity; electronic communication can substitute effectively for in-person meetings when travel costs are prohibitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use asserted technical ignorance to justify mislabeling or misattribution
rubrics_metrics.description: assertions of ignorance of the technical details that one must understand in order to distinguish the modified version ... from the original version do not by any means constitute a justification for participating in the proliferation/citation/dissemination of [the modified false version].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The burden of proof remains on those proposing the modified version; sellers/communicators should not pass off incorrect or mislabelled versions as authentic (analogy with A-product vs X-product).
